The Borderless War

By: ALTYDVRYSTAAT PRODUCTIONS | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The border between Lesotho and the Eastern Free State has disintegrated to such an extent that, in places, it no longer exists.

Unique Selling Point:
*We shoot footage of a normal farmgate that was erected in the border fence. *Drone and/or heli footage of the border *Incredible footage of the Eastern Free State landscape.
*interviews with victims of violent crimes allegedly perpetrated by citizens of Lesotho.

Summary:
South Africans living in small towns along the Eastern Free State’s border with Lesotho are under severe pressure resulting from the disappearing border.
Farm attacks, stock theft (and at least one kidnapping) are real threats in this almost frontier part of the province.
The Free State shares a border of approximately 900km with its mountainous neighbour. How much is compromised?
During a recent visit it was noted that some parts of the fence have totally disappeared.
***The fence is non-existent due to part of it being stolen, criminals moving over the border vandalise, break and cut the fence as well. The entire border fence is damaged and entirely gone in some places.
In one part, on top of Langberg (Near Boesmanskop) a local farmer has erected a gate in the fence. He claims smugglers of stolen vehicles destroy the fence so often, he was left with no other choice.

I spoke to farmers, white and black, last week and the consensus was that the Lesotho border has in fact moved.
Citizens of Lesotho are openly moving their animals to grazing in South Africa. In Wepener, the Lesotho-cattle graze up to the main road. Their Lesotho cattle herders wrapped in traditional blankets and armed with cellphones.
Locals say some taxi routes lead straight over the border and no passport is ever shown or checked.
According to statistics provided by Free State Agriculture, a mere 13 small towns along the border (including 5 in Qwa-Qwa) reported 20% of all the stock theft cases in the entire province for the period of 1 April to 30 June.

In the last six weeks, 20 veldfires was allegedly set around the towns, Hobhouse, Vanstadensrus and Zastron.
***The Freestate agriculture association alleges that the Lesotho locals are purposely setting the fires, their motives are unknown.


Further information:
Case Study:
Interviews with
1. Border farmers (of different races)
2. Afrikaans woman (81) who was attacked, then taken over the border at night and left for dead.
3. Dr. Jane Buys, a risk analyst with Free State Agriculture.
4. Private security and/or farm watch members
5. We will attempt to get somebody from Dept Public Works on camera or at the very least comment.
6. Same with Defence Force.

Script:


V/O
The majestic golden beauty and rugged mountainous sunsets of the Eastern Free State are being overshadowed by slow boiling frustrations fueled by crime and the disappearing Lesotho-border fence.

Derek Link
It may still be an official line on the map but the border between Lesotho and South Africa seems to have disappeared in the Eastern Free State. With the remaining poles just a suggestion of a previous fence. So, one foot in Lesotho, one foot in South Africa.

V/O
Border farmer Tommie Rautenbach has been farming in the Zastron-area for 40 years.
Tommie Die diefstalle eskaleer. Mense raak al hoe meer brutaal. Jy weet selfs ons plaasmense word bang, want hulle word ook geïntimideer.

TRANSLATION
The thefts are escalating. People are getting more brutal. You know, even our farm workers are scared because they are also being intimidated


V/O
While Tommie was speaking, a 22-year old farm manager, Brendin Horner, was being murdered three hours away in Paul Roux.

V/O
This Tuesday the two men accused of Horner’s murder, Sekwetje Mahlamba and Sekola Matlaletsa, briefly appeared in court in Senekal. They were not asked to plead and the matter was postponed.

Farmer Jess de Klerk
We demand that no bail will be granted to these farm attacks and to all violent criminals. We demand that a national taskforce must be set up to investigate stock theft in Paul Roux and surrounding areas.

V/O
A fiery speech by another farmer, André Pienaar, seems to have been the tipping point for some.
Andre Pienaar Mense ons moet dit nou doen. Nou. Daai twee mense sit daarso, ek het hulle gesien man. Wat is hulle? Ek soek nou mannekrag. Ons gaan haal hulle uit.

V/O
Following his speech a group of farmers entered the courthouse building and chaos ensued.


V/O
Pienaar was arrested the following day. On Friday he appeared in court facing charges of malicious damage to property, public violence and terrorism. He is yet to plead.

V/O
Meanwhile in the Eastern Free State, the border fence is causing more problems.

Derek
What is left of the border right now?

Tommie Well the border is a 13 line fence. So it’s easy to pass the border. You just put a stick through the fence and give a few turns and the wire snatch (snaps) and you’re in!

V/O
The ease with which people can cross the border has also opened the door for those with a more criminal intent.

Derek Link
When the smugglers of stolen vehicles break down the border fence on his property on a regular basis a Free State farmer will, as the saying goes, make a plan.

Derek vraag
Tommy this gate is pretty battered and for a good reason I believe?

Tommie
Gesteelde karre het hierdie hek baie gebruik, maar hier kom TLB’s deur, hier kom taxis deur, hier kom groot tipper lorries deur. Dit was op ‘n stadium die hoofpad gewees en as my beeste hier wei dan gaan hulle deur die stukkende draad wat deur die diewe veroorsaak is en dan as my vee aan die ander kant kom, dan word my vee geskut.
TRANSLATION Stolen cars often used this gate, but TLB’s come through here, taxis come through and big tipper lorries. At one stage this was the main road and if my cattle graze here they walk through the broken fence, which was caused by thieves, then my animals are impounded.

VO
PUBLIC WORKS COMMENT Thami Mchunu, national spokesperson for the Department of Public Works and Infrastructure says the fence is in the process of being replaced.

“The Department is currently busy with the funding model for securing funds from the National Treasury,” says Mchunu.

V/O
Tommie is not the only farmer to suffer heavy losses on land neighbouring the missing fence. Hannes Calitz, the owner of the Highlands Safari Lodge, is the fourth generation farming the same land.

Hannes
A while ago I lost quite a lot of cattle, about 15 at a time,

Hannes
Kostegewys, ‘n skaap byvoorbeeld, ‘n ooi wat in produksie is, plus minus R2500. Ek het al oor die afgelope jaar seker oor die 80 verloor. Elande wat ek al baie verloor het ook, toevallig 80 op ‘n slag. Dis ‘n minimum van ‘n koei, sê R5500, ‘n teel koei is tussen R15 000 en R20 000 per bees.
Mens praat van groot bedrae wat verlore gaan. Hulle steel nie klein nie, hulle steel bakkie vragte.
TRANSLATION Cost wise, a sheep is worth more or less R2 500. Over the last year I have lost about 80. I have lost a lot of Eland, coincidentally also 80 at a time, are worth a minimum of R5 500 each. A stud cow is worth R15 000 to R20 000 per head. We speak of large amounts of money that go missing. They don’t steal a little, they steal bakkie loads.

V/O In the Eastern Free State, even the vegetation can be stolen.

Derek link Virtually on a daily basis Lesotho farmers are moving their cattle across the border onto the South African side to enjoy better grazing. But trying to catch them has simply become a dangerous game of cat and mouse.

Derek
Oh so they’ve brought their cattle across to graze?

Hannes
Ja

Derek
But now they're running because they’ve seen you?

Hannes
Ja they are running because they’ve seen me now.

Tommie
You see that's what is happening now.

V/O
In a borrowed Hilux bakkie our team tried to get closer to the illegal grazers.

CHasing scene
Hannes
They put these rocks on the road so we can't go there.

Derek
So they actually try and block you on your own property?

Hannes They block us to give them time to get back. There’s quite a lot here.

Derek Do you have to do this just about every day?

Tommie Ja

Derek That’s crazy.

Tommie Onthou hulle het jare se tyd om dit te doen.

Translated Remember, they have all the time in the world to do this.

Derek Jo! And that’s your wife’s Hilux?

Hannes Ja (laughing).

Derek Jis. She’s gonna love you hey.

Hannes Ja

V/O Farmer Makwena Thola says the herdsmen guarding these animals are not scared to resort to violence.
Mokwena By die nag 12uur hulle kom pla vir my. Die ander het ‘n geweer gehad. Hulle sê hulle soek die bloed van my. Die ander vat die skape daar by die kraal, die nader hulle jaag die beeste, hulle gaan Lesotho toe.
TRANSLATION At midnight they came to bother me. The others had a gun. They said they want my blood. The others took my sheep and some more others chased my cattle to Lesotho.

V/O
Mokwena phoned the police who were too late to catch the intruders. Back in the mountains his assailants made no secret of their intent to return.

Mokwena
Hulle skreeu daar in die berg by daai mense, hulle sê ons soek jou bloed, ons wil jou doodmaak.
TRANSLATION: Those people scream from the mountains. They say: “We want your blood, we want to kill you.”
Derek So you were forced to leave your farm?


Mokwena Ek verloor my plaas van daai mense van Lesotho.
TRANSLATION I lost my farm to those people from Lesotho.

V/O
Dr. Jane Buys, a safety risk analyst for Free State Agriculture, says Mokwena was one of the lucky farmers.

Derek
Jane has there been a rise in the number of attacks along the border area?

Jane
From the first of April in this financial year up until the 31st of August, in the five month period (and it was during lockdown), we had 27 farm attacks in the Free State. That also, it’s inclusive of three murders. And ten of them actually occurred at the border stations.

Derek
Jane do the police have enough equipment, vehicles, personnel?

Jane
I don’t think the police have sufficient capacity in terms of the rural areas. I think the police are really with thousands short in the rural areas.

V/O POLICE COMMENT
Brig. Vish Naido, national police spokesman, says there have always been unique challenges resulting from the porous border. “We are working on special rural initiatives to address the problem,” brig. Naido said.

Derek Link
Isolated and living on farms far apart with a police force that is at most uninspired, the community along the border is left to fend for themselves with some tragic consequences.

V/O
81 year old Daleen van der Hoven and her son Wally live on Wanatha, Tommie’s neighbouring farm. Daleen was home alone one night in June.

Daleen
Toe ek weer my oë oopmaak, toe sit hier ‘n persoon langs my bed en toe ek opkyk staan daar nog drie ander by my voetenent van my bed.

TRANSLATION
When I opened my eyes a man was sitting next to my bed and when I looked up three more were standing by my feet.

V/O
One of the men hit Daleen a devastating blow to the forehead and her nightmare started. They ransacked the house for hours while continuously assaulting her.

Daleen
Toe hulle nou tevrede is met alles wat hulle gevat het, het hulle vir my gesê ek moet uitkom.
TRANSLATION When they were satisfied with everything they took, they told me to come outside.

V/O The
men loaded Daleen and their loot into her own Audi and they drove over Tommie’s farm to the Lesotho border.

Tommie
Ja tannie Daleen is hier afgelaai daai nag wat dit so koud was. Sy het hier opgestap, daar’s ‘n huisie en sy het daar gaan aanklop vir hulp.

TRANSLATION Yes aunt Daleen was dropped off here that night when it was so cold. She walked up here, there is a little house where luckily, somebody we know stays. She went knocking there for help.

Derek
That was Mathato.

Tommie
Dit was Mathato gewees wat haar kom red het, ja.
TRANSLATION It was Mathato who came to save her, yes.

V/O
72-year old Mathato Nkoro, a Lesotho-citizen, lives a stone’s throw away from Tommie’s gate.

Tommie in Sotho Can you explain to me what happened when granny arrived with the car in the night?
TRANSLATION:
Mathato It was around 3, I heard a knock on the window, the person was calling the name; “Mampi, Mampi” And I asked; “who are you? Who is calling me like my boss? Who are you speaking like granny?’
V/O Mathato opened the door to find a battered Daleen, barefoot in temperatures of minus 5 degrees Celsius. She invited her in and called Tommie from a neighbour’s phone, saving Daleen’s life.

Daleen
Ek is nou baie beter, ek wil terug gaan plaas toe.

TRANSLATION I am much better now and want to go back to the farm.

V/O
None of the farmers plan on leaving and even Mokwena would go back to his farm, if given the choice.

Makwena
Daai plaas van my, hy’s mooi. Hy’s mooi, ek like hom, maar daai mense van Lesotho, hulle jaag vir my weg daar. As ek praat met daai storie van plaas my hart seer, ek kry seer. Enige tyd, ek hoor ek kan doodgaan.
TRANSLATION That farm of mine is beautiful. It is beautiful. I like it, but those people from Lesotho, they chased me away from there. If I tell the story of my farm, my heart hurts, I hurt. Any time, I feel like I can just die.

Derek
Do you have sleepless nights that one day you just will have to leave your farm.

Hannes
Ja dis nie onmoontlik nie, maar dit sal maar ‘n tydjie vat om ons hier weg te kry want ons wil nie graag hier weggaan nie.

TRANSLATION
Yes its not impossible but it will take a while to chase us away here because we don’t really want to leave this place.

Tommie
Nee, nee waar sal ek heengaan? Op my ouderdom. Ek is gebore, groot geword. Nee ek gaan daar bly.

TRANSLATION
No, no where will I go? At my age. I was born and raised here. No, I am staying.

PROMO 1:
Emotions in the South African farming community spilled over this week after the senseless murder of the young farm manager, Brendin Horner. In the Eastern Free State, the same storm has been brewing for some time.

PROMO 2:
Belied by the Eastern Free State’s majestic and mountainous beauty, frustrations amongst farmers are growing almost daily with a rise in crime in the areas all along the disappearing border with Lesotho.

PROMO 3:
Stock theft, kidnapping, murder and intimidation are just some of the challenges farmers along South Africa’s border with Lesotho face. This type of growing rural frustrations reached a boiling point this week in Senekal.

Dit was op ‘n stadium die hoofpad gewees en as my beeste hier wei dan gaan hulle deur die stukkende draad wat deur die diewe veroorsaak is en dan as my vee aan die ander kant kom, dan word my vee geskut. TRANSLATION Stolen cars often used this gate, but TLB’s come through here, taxis come through and big tipper lorries. At one stage this was the main road and if my cattle graze here they walk through the broken fence, which was caused by thieves, then my animals are impounded. VO PUBLIC WORKS COMMENT Thami Mchunu, national spokesperson for the Department of Public Works and Infrastructure says the fence is in the process of being replaced. “The Department is currently busy with the funding model for securing funds from the National Treasury,” says Mchunu. V/O Tommie is not the only farmer to suffer heavy losses on land neighbouring the missing fence. Hannes Calitz, the owner of the Highlands Safari Lodge, is the fourth generation farming the same land. Hannes A while ago I lost quite a lot of cattle, about 15 at a time, Hannes Kostegewys, ‘n skaap byvoorbeeld, ‘n ooi wat in produksie is, plus minus R2500. Ek het al oor die afgelope jaar seker oor die 80 verloor. Elande wat ek al baie verloor het ook, toevallig 80 op ‘n slag. Dis ‘n minimum van ‘n koei, sê R5500, ‘n teel koei is tussen R15 000 en R20 000 per bees. Mens praat van groot bedrae wat verlore gaan. Hulle steel nie klein nie, hulle steel bakkie vragte. TRANSLATION Cost wise, a sheep is worth more or less R2 500. Over the last year I have lost about 80. I have lost a lot of Eland, coincidentally also 80 at a time, are worth a minimum of R5 500 each. A stud cow is worth R15 000 to R20 000 per head. We speak of large amounts of money that go missing. They don’t steal a little, they steal bakkie loads. V/O In the Eastern Free State, even the vegetation can be stolen. Derek link Virtually on a daily basis Lesotho farmers are moving their cattle across the border onto the South African side to enjoy better grazing. But trying to catch them has simply become a dangerous game of cat and mouse. Derek Oh so they’ve brought their cattle across to graze? Hannes Ja Derek But now they're running because they’ve seen you? Hannes Ja they are running because they’ve seen me now. Tommie You see that's what is happening now. V/O In a borrowed Hilux bakkie our team tried to get closer to the illegal grazers. CHasing scene Hannes They put these rocks on the road so we can't go there. Derek So they actually try and block you on your own property? Hannes They block us to give them time to get back. There’s quite a lot here. Derek Do you have to do this just about every day? Tommie Ja Derek That’s crazy. Tommie Onthou hulle het jare se tyd om dit te doen. Translated Remember, they have all the time in the world to do this. Derek Jo! And that’s your wife’s Hilux? Hannes Ja (laughing). Derek Jis. She’s gonna love you hey. Hannes Ja V/O Farmer Makwena Thola says the herdsmen guarding these animals are not scared to resort to violence. Mokwena By die nag 12uur hulle kom pla vir my. Die ander het ‘n geweer gehad. Hulle sê hulle soek die bloed van my. Die ander vat die skape daar by die kraal, die nader hulle jaag die beeste, hulle gaan Lesotho toe. TRANSLATION At midnight they came to bother me. The others had a gun. They said they want my blood. The others took my sheep and some more others chased my cattle to Lesotho. V/O Mokwena phoned the police who were too late to catch the intruders. Back in the mountains his assailants made no secret of their intent to return. Mokwena Hulle skreeu daar in die berg by daai mense, hulle sê ons soek jou bloed, ons wil jou doodmaak. TRANSLATION: Those people scream from the mountains. They say: “We want your blood, we want to kill you.” Derek So you were forced to leave your farm? Mokwena Ek verloor my plaas van daai mense van Lesotho. TRANSLATION I lost my farm to those people from Lesotho. V/O Dr. Jane Buys, a safety risk analyst for Free State Agriculture, says Mokwena was one of the lucky farmers. Derek Jane has there been a rise in the number of attacks along the border area? Jane From the first of April in this financial year up until the 31st of August, in the five month period (and it was during lockdown), we had 27 farm attacks in the Free State. That also, it’s inclusive of three murders. And ten of them actually occurred at the border stations. Derek Jane do the police have enough equipment, vehicles, personnel? Jane I don’t think the police have sufficient capacity in terms of the rural areas. I think the police are really with thousands short in the rural areas. V/O POLICE COMMENT Brig. Vish Naido, national police spokesman, says there have always been unique challenges resulting from the porous border. “We are working on special rural initiatives to address the problem,” brig. Naido said. Derek Link Isolated and living on farms far apart with a police force that is at most uninspired, the community along the border is left to fend for themselves with some tragic consequences. V/O 81 year old Daleen van der Hoven and her son Wally live on Wanatha, Tommie’s neighbouring farm. Daleen was home alone one night in June. Daleen Toe ek weer my oë oopmaak, toe sit hier ‘n persoon langs my bed en toe ek opkyk staan daar nog drie ander by my voetenent van my bed. TRANSLATION When I opened my eyes a man was sitting next to my bed and when I looked up three more were standing by my feet. V/O One of the men hit Daleen a devastating blow to the forehead and her nightmare started. They ransacked the house for hours while continuously assaulting her. Daleen Toe hulle nou tevrede is met alles wat hulle gevat het, het hulle vir my gesê ek moet uitkom. TRANSLATION When they were satisfied with everything they took, they told me to come outside. V/O The men loaded Daleen and their loot into her own Audi and they drove over Tommie’s farm to the Lesotho border. Tommie Ja tannie Daleen is hier afgelaai daai nag wat dit so koud was. Sy het hier opgestap, daar’s ‘n huisie en sy het daar gaan aanklop vir hulp. TRANSLATION Yes aunt Daleen was dropped off here that night when it was so cold. She walked up here, there is a little house where luckily, somebody we know stays. She went knocking there for help. Derek That was Mathato. Tommie Dit was Mathato gewees wat haar kom red het, ja. TRANSLATION It was Mathato who came to save her, yes. V/O 72-year old Mathato Nkoro, a Lesotho-citizen, lives a stone’s throw away from Tommie’s gate. Tommie in Sotho Can you explain to me what happened when granny arrived with the car in the night? TRANSLATION: Mathato It was around 3, I heard a knock on the window, the person was calling the name; “Mampi, Mampi” And I asked; “who are you? Who is calling me like my boss? Who are you speaking like granny?’ V/O Mathato opened the door to find a battered Daleen, barefoot in temperatures of minus 5 degrees Celsius. She invited her in and called Tommie from a neighbour’s phone, saving Daleen’s life. Daleen Ek is nou baie beter, ek wil terug gaan plaas toe. TRANSLATION I am much better now and want to go back to the farm. V/O None of the farmers plan on leaving and even Mokwena would go back to his farm, if given the choice. Makwena Daai plaas van my, hy’s mooi. Hy’s mooi, ek like hom, maar daai mense van Lesotho, hulle jaag vir my weg daar. As ek praat met daai storie van plaas my hart seer, ek kry seer. Enige tyd, ek hoor ek kan doodgaan. TRANSLATION That farm of mine is beautiful. It is beautiful. I like it, but those people from Lesotho, they chased me away from there. If I tell the story of my farm, my heart hurts, I hurt. Any time, I feel like I can just die. Derek Do you have sleepless nights that one day you just will have to leave your farm. Hannes Ja dis nie onmoontlik nie, maar dit sal maar ‘n tydjie vat om ons hier weg te kry want ons wil nie graag hier weggaan nie. TRANSLATION Yes its not impossible but it will take a while to chase us away here because we don’t really want to leave this place. Tommie Nee, nee waar sal ek heengaan? Op my ouderdom. Ek is gebore, groot geword. Nee ek gaan daar bly. TRANSLATION No, no where will I go? At my age. I was born and raised here. No, I am staying. PROMO 1: Emotions in the South African farming community spilled over this week after the senseless murder of the young farm manager, Brendin Horner. In the Eastern Free State, the same storm has been brewing for some time. PROMO 2: Belied by the Eastern Free State’s majestic and mountainous beauty, frustrations amongst farmers are growing almost daily with a rise in crime in the areas all along the disappearing border with Lesotho. PROMO 3: Stock theft, kidnapping, murder and intimidation are just some of the challenges farmers along South Africa’s border with Lesotho face. This type of growing rural frustrations reached a boiling point this week in Senekal.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The border between Lesotho and the Eastern Free State has disintegrated to such an extent that, in places, it no longer exists.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: *We shoot footage of a normal farmgate that was erected in the border fence. *Drone and/or heli footage of the border *Incredible footage of the Eastern Free State landscape. *interviews with victims of violent crimes allegedly perpetrated by citizens of Lesotho.
metadata.Summary: South Africans living in small towns along the Eastern Free State’s border with Lesotho are under severe pressure resulting from the disappearing border. Farm attacks, stock theft (and at least one kidnapping) are real threats in this almost frontier part of the province. The Free State shares a border of approximately 900km with its mountainous neighbour. How much is compromised? During a recent visit it was noted that some parts of the fence have totally disappeared. ***The fence is non-existent due to part of it being stolen, criminals moving over the border vandalise, break and cut the fence as well. The entire border fence is damaged and entirely gone in some places. In one part, on top of Langberg (Near Boesmanskop) a local farmer has erected a gate in the fence. He claims smugglers of stolen vehicles destroy the fence so often, he was left with no other choice. I spoke to farmers, white and black, last week and the consensus was that the Lesotho border has in fact moved. Citizens of Lesotho are openly moving their animals to grazing in South Africa. In Wepener, the Lesotho-cattle graze up to the main road. Their Lesotho cattle herders wrapped in traditional blankets and armed with cellphones. Locals say some taxi routes lead straight over the border and no passport is ever shown or checked. According to statistics provided by Free State Agriculture, a mere 13 small towns along the border (including 5 in Qwa-Qwa) reported 20% of all the stock theft cases in the entire province for the period of 1 April to 30 June. In the last six weeks, 20 veldfires was allegedly set around the towns, Hobhouse, Vanstadensrus and Zastron. ***The Freestate agriculture association alleges that the Lesotho locals are purposely setting the fires, their motives are unknown.
